props.gloss_en: Rav Huna: one who slaughtered with a knife later found notched -- even if he broke bones with it all day -- the slaughter is invalid
Rav Huna's reason: we are concerned that perhaps it was notched on the hide
Rav Chisda: the slaughter is valid
Rav Chisda's reason: perhaps it was notched on the bone
Rav Huna (9a): an animal in its lifetime stands in a presumption of prohibition until you know how it was slaughtered
a bone certainly notches, hide may or may not; it is doubt against certainty, and a doubt does not remove a certainty
one immersed and an interposition was found on him -- even if he handled that kind all day, the immersion fails until he says 'I am sure it was not on me before'
the knife was flawed; the animal was not flawed
the baraita: he cut the gullet and afterwards the windpipe was displaced -- valid
the windpipe was displaced and afterwards he cut the gullet -- invalid
where he does not know whether the windpipe was displaced before or after -- that was the case, and they said: every doubt in slaughter is invalid
'every doubt in slaughter' -- does it not come to include a case like this one (the notched knife)?
no -- it comes to include a doubt whether he paused or pressed
there (pausing / pressing) the flaw arose in the animal
the halakha follows Rav Huna where he broke no bone with it: invalid
the halakha follows Rav Chisda where he broke a bone with it: valid
by implication Rav Chisda holds it valid even where he broke no bone
on what was it notched? -- say: on the neck-bone
there was a case, and Rav Yosef declared as many as thirteen animals tereifot
Rav Yosef acted in accordance with Rav Huna (forbidding even the first animal)
no -- in accordance with Rav Chisda, and all but the first were forbidden
for were it per Rav Chisda -- since we merely attribute the notch, why to the first animal's neck-bone? perhaps it was the last's
Rav Kahana required checking the knife between each and every slaughter
per Rav Huna, to invalidate the earlier animal?
no -- per Rav Chisda, to validate the later ones
one witness is believed in matters of prohibition
R' Yochanan: they required showing the knife to a sage only out of the sage's honour
establish a matter on its presumptive status
Lev 14:38 -- the priest leaves the house and quarantines it; perhaps as he left the mark shrank below its size! rather, because we say: establish it on its presumption
Rav Acha bar Yaakov: perhaps he exits walking backwards, seeing the mark as he goes
the mishna: in a dark house one does not open windows to see its mark
the mishna (Yoma): the High Priest exited and came out the way he had entered (facing inward)
the baraita: not from his own house ('to the entrance'), not under the lintel ('from the house') -- he stands beside the lintel and quarantines
and if he went into his own house, or stood inside the house, and quarantined -- his quarantine holds: 'and he shall quarantine the house', in any case
from where?! it is written 'after the majority to incline' (Ex 23:2)
a majority before us -- nine shops, the Sanhedrin -- is not in question
follow the majority -- including a majority not before us, as with a minor boy and girl
R' Elazar: from the head of the olah, which is not cut into pieces ('it into its pieces, not its pieces into pieces') -- let us fear the brain membrane was pierced! rather, we follow the majority
Mar breih deRavina: from the ban on breaking a bone of the Pesach (Ex 12:46) -- let us fear the brain membrane was pierced! rather, we follow the majority
the baraita: one who cuts the sinews or burns the bones [of the Pesach] does not violate breaking a bone
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: from the fat-tail, which must be whole (Lev 3:9) -- let us fear the spinal cord was severed! rather, we follow the majority
Rav Sheshet breih deRav Idi: from the egla arufa, which must be whole but for its broken neck -- let us fear it is a tereifa! rather, we follow the majority
devei R' Yannai: atonement is written of it, as of sacrifices
Rabba bar Rav Sheila: from the red heifer, burned whole as it was slaughtered whole -- let us fear it is a tereifa! rather, we follow the majority
Rav Acha bar Yaakov: from the scapegoat -- the two goats must be equal; let us fear one is a tereifa! rather, we follow the majority
the mishna (Yoma): it had not reached halfway down the mountain before it was torn limb from limb
Rav Mari: from one who strikes his father or mother, whom the Torah executes -- let us fear he is not his father! rather, we follow the majority: most intercourse is the husband's
Rav Kahana: from the murderer, whom the Torah executes -- let us fear the victim was a tereifa! rather, we follow the majority
Ravina: from conspiring witnesses (Deut 19:19) -- let us fear the man they testified against was a tereifa! rather, we follow the majority
Beribbi: if they have not yet killed, they are killed; if they killed, they are not killed
Rav Ashi: from slaughter itself -- 'slaughter and eat'; let us fear he cut at the place of a hole! rather, we follow the majority
perhaps where it is possible [to check] it is required; where it is not possible, not -- the majority is relied on only where checking is impossible
R' Meir is concerned for the minority
Pesach and sacrifices [which must be eaten] -- what is there to say? so even for R' Meir: where possible it is required, where impossible not
